parsed.rationale: Both `PlaybackController` (line 27) and `AudioPlayerProtocol` (line 19) in the `Playback` package share six structurally identical or near-identical members: `installRenderTap:()`, `removeRenderTap:()`, `isPlaying:Bool`, `makeAudioBufferStream:() -> AsyncStream<AVAudioPCMBuffer>`, `play:()` (modulo the `reason:` label on `PlaybackController`), and `stop:()` (same caveat). Extracting these into a new parent protocol `AudioPlaybackCore` within the same `Shared/Playback/Sources/PlaybackCore/Protocols/` directory eliminates the duplication while preserving the divergent members: `PlaybackController` retains `isLoading:Bool`, `toggle:(reason:)`, and the `PlaybackReason`-parameterised signatures, while `AudioPlayerProtocol` retains `eventStream:AsyncStream<AudioPlayerInternalEvent>`, `stateStream:AsyncStream<PlayerState>`, and its unparameterised `play:()`/`stop:()`. Neither record carries any restraint flag (`is_test`, `is_mock`, `is_sample_app`, `is_codegen` are all false), so the refactor is safe to pursue. The differing `state` property types (`PlaybackState` vs `PlayerState`) mean `state` should remain in each child unless those types are also unified.
